text: Continuous Integration (CI) is a common practice in modern software development. It means that developers regularly add their code to a shared repository. After each change, an automated build starts. This build compiles the code and runs tests to check that everything works correctly. The main goal is catching issues early, before they become big problems. CI pipelines make this process smooth and repeatable. They can automatically build, test, and even deploy the software. By using CI, teams save time, reduce mistakes, and deliver better software faster. It has become an essential part of professional development workflows.
